clue.text: Fellow connected with the Spanish church

parts.note: a fellow is a chap
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A man is linked with a church in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel is a small place of Christian worship, so a kind of church.

clue.text: Row of bushes in verge below hospital

indicators.note: below, in a down clue, sends the word for verge underneath, so second

parts.note: a verge is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A hedge grows on the verge beneath a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedge is a line of closely planted shrubs forming a boundary.

clue.text: Publicity for movement

definitions.meaning: advertising and marketing to raise awareness
a move upward in rank or to a higher league

explanation.surface: Publicity for a political movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Promotion is both publicising a product and advancement to a higher position.

clue.text: Bloomer at university contributing to endless row

indicators.note: contributing to means put into the middle of the shortened word
endless means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a row is a line
to be up is to be in residence at university, a British usage

explanation.surface: A gaffe at university adds to a never-ending argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A lupin is a flowering plant, and a bloomer here means something that blooms.

clue.text: What a nark may do is endless?

definitions.meaning: a nark is a police informer, who may warn the police in advance
with the tip taken off, a thing has lost its end

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what an informer does.
explanation.definitionFit: To tip off is to give secret advance warning, and something with its tip off has had its end removed.

clue.text: Drake, thus, spliced decorative knot

indicators.note: spliced, a rope-work term, says the letters are interwoven into a new order

explanation.surface: Sir Francis Drake ties a fancy knot in a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A Turk's head is an ornamental knot woven in a rope, resembling a turban.

clue.text: Stick to" "administer severe beating

definitions.meaning: to glue something onto a surface

explanation.surface: Two instructions: glue it and give a thrashing.
explanation.definitionFit: Paste means both to fix with glue and, informally, to beat soundly.

clue.text: Fail to meet brief after defeat

indicators.note: after places the word for brief behind the word for defeat

parts.note: a fall is a defeat, as of a city
brief means short

explanation.surface: Someone fails to meet a brief after a defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall short is an idiom for failing to reach a target or standard.

clue.text: Film king

definitions.meaning: A 1981 comedy film starring Dudley Moore
the legendary British king of the Round Table

explanation.surface: A film about a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a well-known comedy film and to the legendary king of Camelot.

clue.text: Mean to defraud Treasury, ultimately

parts.note: a sting is a swindle, so to sting is to defraud

indicators.note: ultimately picks out the final letter of treasury

explanation.surface: Someone means to cheat the Treasury in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingy means miserly, the adjective sense of mean.

clue.text: Was up on bronco's back in Wild West Show

parts.note: to be up on a horse is to ride it, so past tense rode

indicators.note: the back of the word bronco's is its final letter

explanation.surface: A rider sat astride a bucking horse in a cowboy show.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is an exhibition of cowboy skills, the classic Wild West show.

clue.text: Left most of toast and cheese

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: most of the word means it loses its final letter

parts.note: a toast to someone is a salute

explanation.surface: Someone left most of their toast but ate the cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Port Salut is a mild French cheese originally made by Trappist monks.

clue.text: Dance? Husband's terribly wooden

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of wooden are badly arranged and must be reworked

explanation.surface: A wife complains her husband dances very stiffly.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoedown is a lively American folk dance or the social gathering where it is held.

clue.text: Hat put back on after conclusion of matins

indicators.note: after says the word on comes after the preceding letter

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's instruction to restore a deleted word, putting it back

indicators.note: the conclusion of matins is its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone put their hat back on after the end of the morning service.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stetson is a broad-brimmed cowboy hat, named after its American maker.

clue.text: Understood about blocking plan to send down student

indicators.note: blocking means sitting inside and stopping up the word for plan

parts.note: a ruse is a crafty plan

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the word for understood round

parts.note: something understood without being said is tacit

explanation.surface: A tacit scheme to expel a student from university.
explanation.walkthrough: To rusticate is old British university slang: the student is sent to the country, away from college, for a term or more.
explanation.definitionFit: To rusticate is the British university term for suspending a student and sending them away temporarily.

clue.text: Dope easy to name

parts.note: easy means simple

explanation.surface: A drug that is easy to identify.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for a fool, which a simpleton is.

clue.text: Artist imprisoned by a bitter twisted judge

indicators.note: imprisoned by means locked inside the other letters
twisted means the letters are contorted into a fresh order

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: An artist is jailed by an embittered, warped judge.
explanation.definitionFit: To arbitrate is to judge a dispute as an impartial referee, both verbs.

clue.text: Lie level, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word that is said out loud sounding like another

parts.note: a level of a building is a storey

explanation.surface: A level sounds like it is lying flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A story is a fib or untruth, as when a child is told not to tell stories.

clue.text: Boffin in tests spread across Channel Islands

indicators.note: across means stretched over and around the inner letters
spread means the letters are scattered into another arrangement

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands, off the coast of France

explanation.surface: A researcher runs experiments throughout Jersey and Guernsey.
explanation.definitionFit: Boffin is British slang for a scientist or technical expert.

clue.text: Fruit from Spanish province marketer initially imported

indicators.note: imported means brought inside the province's name

parts.note: León is a province in north-west Spain

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of marketer

explanation.surface: Fruit from a Spanish province brought in by a trader.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemon is a sour yellow citrus fruit.

clue.text: The French boy's Bible reading

parts.note: les is a French word for the, plural
a boy is a son

explanation.surface: A French lad's passage read from scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson is a passage from the Bible read aloud in a church service.

clue.text: Foul by new forward in game

parts.note: foul means bad
mint means brand new, as in mint condition
on means forward, as in moving on

explanation.surface: A player commits a foul by a newcomer moving forward in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket sport played with a shuttlecock over a net.

clue.text: Took care of shark close to land

parts.note: the nurse shark is a species of shark

indicators.note: close to means the last letter of the word land

explanation.surface: A shark was looked after when it came near land.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursed means tended or looked after a patient.

clue.text: 'Betrayal', a complete success at the box office?

definitions.meaning: a betrayal of principles or allies

definitions.text: a complete success at the box office?
definitions.meaning: a show for which every ticket has been bought

explanation.surface: A film called Betrayal fills every seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sell-out is both a betrayal of one's side and an event whose tickets are all gone.

clue.text: Oxygen needed by enormous Greek character

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
mega is slang for huge

explanation.surface: A huge Greek needs breathing apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: What's in bottle perhaps given a right shaking?

indicators.note: a shaking jumbles the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A bottle's contents are given a vigorous shake.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinegar is a sour liquid condiment often sold in bottles, so an example of bottled contents.

clue.text: Steward may be very late, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong with the letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A steward may turn up very late, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: A valet is a manservant who attends to a gentleman, a personal steward.

clue.text: Grind and cut small number inside

indicators.note: inside places the number within the word for cut

parts.note: a gash is a deep cut
N stands for an unspecified small number in maths

explanation.surface: Grind something and slice a few pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To gnash is to grind the teeth together.

clue.text: Aware of things, like the footballer about to pass?

definitions.text: like the footballer about to pass?
definitions.meaning: a footballer about to pass has the ball at their feet

explanation.surface: An alert footballer is about to pass the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: On the ball is an idiom for alert and well-informed; literally, a player poised to pass is on it.

clue.text: Picture that is framing periodical

indicators.note: framing means the first piece goes around the second like a frame

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation for that is (id est)
a periodical is a mag, short for magazine

explanation.surface: A picture is framing a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or likeness.

clue.text: Wearing box, as a precaution

parts.note: to be in clothes is to be wearing them
a case is a box or container

explanation.surface: A cricketer wears a protective box just to be safe.
explanation.definitionFit: In case is an idiom meaning as a safeguard against something happening.

clue.text: The City? I dropped out, being grumpy

indicators.note: out signals the remaining letters are put out of order
dropped means the letter is removed from the phrase

explanation.surface: Someone quit their City job and is now irritable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' removes I from THE CITY, leaving THECTY, which 'out' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetchy means irritable and bad-tempered, a synonym of grumpy.
